# AuraTrack 6.1 report inventory (the M5 baseline)

**Status: draft from the 6.1 code** (`src/reports/` in AuraTrack-v6). Reference output generated 2026-10-31; the draft has not yet been checked section by section against it.

**Visual reference:** reports generated by the 6.1 app from **made-up test data** are saved in `docs/plan/reports-6.1/` (see its README; regenerate with `node scripts/gen-6x-reference.mjs`). They show the exact 6.1 look without any personal data.
- Real medical data (your own reports, backups) is **never** committed. `.gitignore` blocks `*.atbak` and `docs/plan/reports-6.1/real/`.
- Comparisons with your real data happen only on your computer.

Rule for M5: first rebuild every section exactly as below, compare with 6.1 output from the same data, then add the improvements you approve.

## R-1 Neurologist report (PDF and HTML preview), for a chosen date range
In page order:
1. **Header:** AuraTrack brand, report title, generated date, period, patient (name, date of birth if enabled), reporter (carer or self), neurologist, institution and contact.
2. **Meta cards:**
   - Patient: name, date of birth, emergency contact.
   - Report summary: number of seizures in the period, period length, average duration.
3. **Stat cards (4):** seizures in the period, average duration, days with seizures, number of seizure types.
4. **Current medications:** each active medication with dose summary, schedule and per-slot doses.
5. **Medication changes in the period:** a table of date, medication, change type, from → to, note.
6. **Recent seizures (latest N):** date, time, type, duration.
7. **Medication context:** adherence counts (taken, late, assumed, missed) per medication.
8. **Clinical context cards:**
   - awareness levels
   - recovery and after-seizure findings (the most frequent findings)
   - rescue medication use
   - triggers and medications (report notes)
9. **Wellbeing context:** days covered, mood distribution, factors present on seizure days compared with other days.
10. **Clinical flags:** seizures at or over the alert time; reported triggers (top 5, with "also logged in that day's wellbeing"); the emergency plan rule used.
11. **Trend analysis (charts):**
    - seizure frequency (bars per day; long seizures marked; alert-time legend)
    - duration trend (line, with an alert-time reference line)
    - wellbeing correlation
    - type breakdown
    - phase breakdown (aura, seizure and recovery, stacked, for the last 10)
12. **Condensed event details:** a card per selected seizure (the latest 3, plus all long or edited ones) with phases, symptoms, after-seizure findings, triggers, notes, video file name and badges (≥ alert time, auto-stopped, edited).
13. **Ictal symptom log:** symptoms grouped, with path, medical term and location.
14. **Data quality and confidence:** fully recorded, partly recorded and untagged counts, with a confidence level.

## R-2 Event log (PDF), for a date range
A table of date, time, type, duration and notes for every seizure, followed by the medication changes table.

## R-3 Monthly seizure diary (PDF), for a month
A calendar grid with seizures per day (type and duration markers, trigger marker), a legend, the medications and medication changes that month, and a footer.

## R-4 EEG diary (PDF), per session
Session details (title, start, planned and actual end, notes), then the activities and seizure references in time order, with durations and moods.

## R-5 CSV export, for a date range
Seizures (id, date, time, type, duration, notes, after-seizure findings with areas, paralysis areas, recovery), medications, dose logs, medication changes, wellbeing entries with factors, and EEG sessions and activities.

## Shared behaviour
- Every text is in the chosen language (9 languages).
- **Save:** through the system save dialog where available, otherwise a download; file names carry the local date.
- **Print preview** in the app.
- **Charts** are SVG, rendered into the PDF.
